Predict from a Distance-Removal Model with a Fixed-Range Abundance Field

Source: R/gdr_response_field_predict.R
predict-unmarkedFitGDRField-method.Rd

Predict density, the distance scale or the removal probability from a model fitted by fit_gdr_response_field(). Abundance predictions include the fitted field, at fitted blocks or at new projected locations, and their standard errors include the field's uncertainty.

Usage

# S4 method for class 'unmarkedFitGDRField'
predict(
  object,
  type = "lambda",
  newdata = NULL,
  backTransform = TRUE,
  na.rm = TRUE,
  appendData = FALSE,
  level = 0.95,
  re.form = NULL,
  coords = NULL,
  crs = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

An unmarkedFitGDRField returned by fit_gdr_response_field().

type

Character. The model component to predict: "lambda" (density, the default), "dist" (distance scale) or "rem" (removal probability). "state" is accepted as another name for "lambda".

newdata

A data frame of covariate values, or an unmarkedFrameGDR with the fitted survey protocol (one visit, the same distance bands and the same interval lengths). The default NULL predicts for the rows used in fitting. Transformations, factor levels and spline bases keep their definitions from fitting. With the default, removal predictions have one row per survey and removal interval.

backTransform

Logical, default TRUE. TRUE returns density per square kilometer, the distance scale in meters or the removal probability per unit of interval time. FALSE returns the link scale (log, log or logit).

na.rm

Logical, default TRUE. Kept for compatibility with unmarked. Rows with missing predictor values are not dropped. They stop the prediction, so remove them first.

appendData

Logical, default FALSE. If TRUE, the prediction columns are added to the right of the prediction rows.

level

Confidence level between 0 and 1, default 0.95. NULL skips the limits, which are then returned as NA.

re.form

NULL (default) includes the fitted field, and any observer intercepts in the distance component. NA sets all of them to zero. A zero-field prediction describes a block with no deviation. It is not an average over blocks.

coords

Optional two-column matrix or data frame of projected coordinates for abundance predictions at new locations, one row per row of newdata. The default NULL locates each row by its level of the grouping factor (for example block = "b3"), which must be a fitted level.

crs

The CRS of coords, as an EPSG code or other input accepted by sf::st_crs(). Required with coords. It must equal the CRS used in fitting, because coordinates are never transformed.

...

Not used. Unrecognized arguments stop the prediction.

Value

A data frame with one row per prediction row:

  • Predicted: the prediction on the scale set by backTransform.

  • SE: its standard error on the same scale. Back-transformed SEs use the delta method.

  • lower, upper: confidence limits at level, computed on the link scale and then back-transformed, so they are not symmetric around Predicted.

The attribute response_field_uncertainty explains the SE. Its element fitted_joint_predictor_variance is the link-scale variance from the fitted coefficients and field. new_field_residual_predictor_variance is the extra link-scale variance at new locations (zero at fitted blocks). SE_includes_new_field_residual is TRUE when any row has that extra variance. omitted lists what the SE leaves out: observation noise and uncertainty in the ecological scales and the range.

Choose where to predict

For abundance, each prediction needs a field value. A row whose grouping factor names a fitted block uses that block's fitted deviation. A row with a location in coords uses the field value predicted at that location from the fitted block deviations. At a fitted block location this equals the block's own deviation. Far from all blocks, compared with the range, it shrinks toward zero. For raster maps, use response_field_geometry() with predict.multiScaleR() instead of calling this method cell by cell.

For type = "dist" with an observer random intercept, rows must name fitted observers unless re.form = NA.

What the standard errors include

The SE combines two link-scale variances. The first comes from the joint covariance of the fitted coefficients and field values, including their cross-covariances. The second applies only at new locations. It is the field variance left after conditioning on the fitted blocks, evaluated at the estimated field SD. It is zero at a fitted block and grows toward the full field variance far from all blocks. Neither variance is observation noise, so these are confidence intervals for the expected value, not prediction intervals for a new count.

A density prediction is exp() of the linear predictor at the fitted field values. It is not the average density over possible field values. The intervals treat the ecological scales of effect and the correlation range as known.

See also

fit_gdr_response_field(), make_gdr_refitter()

Examples

# \donttest{
# The field needs unmarked 1.5.2 and TMB 1.9.25.
if (requireNamespace("TMB", quietly = TRUE) &&
    utils::packageVersion("unmarked") == "1.5.2" &&
    utils::packageVersion("TMB") == "1.9.25") {
  # Eight survey blocks 1 km apart, six point counts in each
  block <- factor(rep(paste0("b", 1:8), each = 6))
  hab <- rep(seq(-1, 1, length.out = 6), 8)
  shift <- c(-0.4, -0.3, -0.1, 0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.35, 0.4)[block]
  sim <- sim_dat_gdr(density = exp(log(400) + 0.5 * hab + shift),
    distance_scale = 40, removal = 0.2, dist_breaks = c(0, 25, 50, 75),
    interval_lengths = c(2, 3, 5), interval_units = "minutes",
    site_covs = data.frame(hab = hab, block = block), seed = 1)
  template <- unmarked::gdistremoval(lambdaformula = ~ hab + (1 | block),
    removalformula = ~ 1, distanceformula = ~ 1, data = sim$observed,
    keyfun = "halfnorm", mixture = "P", output = "density",
    unitsOut = "kmsq", K = 60, engine = "TMB",
    starts = c(log(400), 0, log(40), qlogis(0.2), log(0.3)))
  block_xy <- cbind(x = 500000 + 1000 * (as.integer(block) - 1),
                    y = 4400000)
  rownames(block_xy) <- rownames(unmarked::siteCovs(sim$observed))
  cold <- c("beta_lambda[1]" = log(300), "beta_lambda[2]" = 0,
            "beta_dist[1]" = log(30), "beta_rem[1]" = qlogis(0.4),
            "lsigma_lambda[1]" = log(0.5))
  settings <- list(method = "BFGS", se = TRUE, threads = 1L,
                   control = list(maxit = 2500L, reltol = 1e-10))
  field_fit <- fit_gdr_response_field(template, block_xy, crs = 32617,
    range = 2000, cold_starts = list(cold = cold),
    audit_dir = tempfile("gdr-field-"), tmb_settings = settings)

  # Density (birds per square km) at average habitat: in block b3, at a
  # point halfway between blocks b3 and b4, and with the field set to zero
  in_block <- predict(field_fit, type = "lambda",
    newdata = data.frame(hab = 0, block = factor("b3", levels(block))))
  between <- predict(field_fit, type = "lambda",
    newdata = data.frame(hab = 0), coords = cbind(502500, 4400000),
    crs = 32617)
  no_field <- predict(field_fit, type = "lambda",
    newdata = data.frame(hab = 0), re.form = NA)
  dens <- rbind(in_block, between, no_field)
  rownames(dens) <- c("block b3", "between b3 and b4", "no field")
  print(dens)
  # The SE between blocks adds field variance left after conditioning on
  # the fitted blocks (both variances on the log scale)
  u <- attr(between, "response_field_uncertainty")
  print(c(fitted = unname(u$fitted_joint_predictor_variance),
          between_blocks = unname(u$new_field_residual_predictor_variance)))
  # Removal probability per minute, one row per survey and interval
  print(head(predict(field_fit, type = "rem"), 3))
}
#>                   Predicted        SE    lower    upper
#> block b3           378.4863  85.53074 243.0495 589.3939
#> between b3 and b4  423.9838  94.82578 273.5107 657.2402
#> no field           459.1513 100.73197 298.6847 705.8276
#>         fitted between_blocks
